messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: runtime-serving-prod route=text.generate — sudden tail latency increase and 5xx spike, paging #eng-oncall (severity=P2)

maria (oncall): ack, oncall here :eyes: starting triage — pulling Grafana and traces

support-bot: FYI support queue: two customers reported realtime failures (AcmeCRM ticket #11203, StripeFlow ticket #11204). Tickets show timeouts ~10–20s

jon (eng): looking at canary hosts — prefetch eviction rate jumped ~8x on canary-12 group, KV cache miss rate ~89% on those nodes

kevin (runtime): rooting around in logs — lots of "kernel fallback to scalar" messages and microbatch window shrinking; suspect new kernel selector rule in rollout 9a7b2c

aya (sre): can we throttle canary traffic to limit blast radius while we investigate? suggest set canary weight -> 5%

maria (oncall): doing traffic slice reduction now
`/routing set-weight runtime.canary-12 0.05 --reason "emergency oncall throttle"`

incident-bot: ROUTING: runtime.canary-12 weight set to 0.05 by maria (oncall) — traffic shifted off canary (10s)

jon (eng): after traffic shift, latency on prod aggregated down from 240ms p95 -> 110ms, but canary nodes still showing high token latency and scalar kernel fallback persists

kevin (runtime): safe mitigation: flip kernel selector flag back to previous path for canary-12, and enable kill-switch for prefetch-v2 rollout. doing kernel flip now:
```
/infra feature-flag set runtime.kernel_selector_v2 false --scope canary-12 --by kevin
/infra feature-flag set prefetch-v2.kill_switch true --by kevin
```

aya (sre): before full rollback, recommend reverting commit that introduced selector rule to avoid repeated thrash — can we push quick rollback?

jon (eng): preparing rollback: `git revert --no-edit 9a7b2c` then deploying to canary slice to validate

maria (oncall): please coordinate deploy and confirm health checks. support — prepare short customer note in case we need public comms

support-bot: Draft message ready: "We're aware of degraded latency for some realtime requests; we've throttled the canary and are rolling back a recent change. We'll provide updates in 30 minutes."

kevin (runtime): rollback applied to canary-12, health checks green. kernel flag already flipped. Observability: KV miss rate dropping, batcher window slowly recovering

incident-bot: METRIC UPDATE: p95 latency prod route down to 95ms (from 240ms), 5xx rate back to baseline (0.2%) — alert volume decreasing

jon (eng): verified token/s throughput returning to normal on canary hosts. batching re-enabled on 80% of nodes. will monitor for regression for 1 hour

aya (sre): re-enabled aggressive autoscaling thresholds we had relaxed during the spike. will keep an eye on eviction churn and memory pressure

maria (oncall): handoff — oncall-night please take post-rollback watch. @jon you own 30m active monitoring then hand to night. leave a short runbook note in the incident channel

jon (eng): ack. will monitor traces, KV miss, and kernel fallback logs. opening postmortem ticket IT-1982 and will add timeline

support-bot: Support notified customers (AcmeCRM, StripeFlow) with the drafted note. will escalate if we see additional error reports :thumbsup:

maria (oncall): closing paging loop for now — continuing monitoring and prep for postmortem. great quick coordination team.

jon (eng): quick notes to add to postmortem: reproduce steps, selector test coverage gap, add synthetic for prefetch eviction, add alert rule for "scalar-kernel-fallback" spikes

aya (sre): adding runbook step: on scalar fallback spike -> throttle canary + flip kernel flag + rollback candidate commit; include exact CLI commands we ran

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated. will convert to postmortem and follow-up tasks assigned.
